title: What enforcement found about officials
question: Which supervisors and mayors, or committees carrying their names, appear in an Ethics Commission penalty, a City Attorney action or a federal case?
finding: The Ethics Commission’s register of penalties lists 22 resolved cases naming 13 of the 36 officials or a committee carrying their name, with $207,033 in penalties; the largest is $108,180 on 2024-11-08 (Mayor Mark Farrell for Yes on Prop D, Mark Farrell for Mayor 2024, Mark Farrell, and Roy Herrera). 17 of them are filed under “Campaign Finance”. Of 179 City Attorney actions, federal charging papers, pleas and probable-cause findings in this project’s document library, 0 name a roster official as a subject. 15 of the project’s own case files name one.
how: Every row of the Ethics Commission’s published register of enforcement penalties whose respondents include an official on the roster, or a committee whose name carries the official’s first and last name; duplicated register rows are shown once. The words in quotation marks are the first twelve words of the register’s own description of the violation. The document library’s index is searched by subject for City Attorney actions, federal complaints, indictments, pleas and Ethics probable-cause findings. Project case files are listed after the register rows, with the tier each file assigns.
limits: A stipulated penalty is an admitted or agreed violation of a specific rule and says nothing beyond that rule: 11 of the 22 rows cite advertising disclaimers and 3 cite record-keeping. 3 rows concern a committee formed by others that carries the official’s name; the “who” column says which. Being connected is not being corrupt, and the absence of a case is not a finding of good conduct: the register lists only cases that ended in a penalty, so a complaint that was dismissed or is still open does not appear in it.
